high.title: Foreign Capital Flight from B3: May Sees First Monthly Outflow from International Investors
high.summary: Foreign investors withdrew R$13.8 billion from B3 in May, marking the first monthly net outflow after four consecutive months of positive inflows that totaled over R$26.5 billion in January alone. This dramatic reversal from the strong foreign appetite earlier in 2026 reflects deteriorating domestic conditions combined with external pressures from Middle East conflicts affecting global inflation expectations and interest rate trajectories. The capital flight represents a significant shift in investor sentiment toward Brazilian assets, with analysts pointing to persistent geopolitical tensions and worsening domestic environment as key drivers. For BRL traders, this outflow trend signals potential continued pressure on the Real, while bond investors should monitor whether this capital flight accelerates, potentially forcing BCB intervention or affecting government bond yields. The magnitude of the reversal—from R$26.5B inflow in January to R$13.8B outflow in May—suggests a fundamental reassessment of Brazil risk premium.

high.title: Petrobras and Prio Lead Ibovespa Higher on Middle East War Impact
high.summary: Petrobras (PETR3/PETR4) and Prio (PRIO3) shares surged as oil companies led Ibovespa gains following escalating US-Iran tensions. Brent crude futures jumped 7.11% to $97.57/barrel while WTI soared 8.36% to $94.61/barrel after US attacks on Iranian military installations over the weekend. This geopolitical premium in oil prices directly benefits Brazilian oil producers and could provide some support to the Real through improved trade balance dynamics, though the broader market impact remains mixed given simultaneous foreign capital outflows from Brazilian equities.

medium.title: Vale Falls Over 2% as Metal Commodities Weaken
medium.summary: Vale (VALE3) dropped 2.63% to R$80.64, dragging down the Ibovespa as iron ore futures declined in Dalian (-0.19%) and Singapore (-0.80%). The mining sector selloff, led by CSN's 7.45% plunge, reflects both commodity weakness and foreign investor flight from Brazilian equities amid rising global risk aversion.

medium.title: "Sell in May": Ibovespa Posts Worst Monthly Performance in 3 Years
medium.summary: The Ibovespa fell approximately 6% in May, marking its worst monthly decline since 2023. The selloff was driven by persistent inflation concerns, political noise, and adverse external conditions, validating the "sell in May" market adage for Brazilian equities.

medium.title: Japan's Massive FX Intervention Fails to Sustainably Weaken Dollar vs Yen, Says ING
medium.summary: Japan spent $73.5 billion in April-May FX intervention, the largest since 2004, temporarily pushing USD/JPY from above 160 to below 156, though the pair has since rebounded to 159.71. This highlights challenges faced by central banks attempting to counter strong dollar trends, with potential implications for other emerging market central banks including Brazil's BCB.
